title: Composed Majority Error Above Half
statement: Fix $p\in(1/2,1)$. For each $m$, take two independent signs and an independent block of $2m+1$ signs, all with probability $p$ of being $-1$. First take the majority sign of the block, then take the majority of that sign and the two initial signs. The probability that the resulting sign is $-1$ tends, as $m\to\infty$, to $1-(1-p)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: The block size is $2m+1$ with $m$ tending to infinity
All signs are independent and each is $-1$ with probability $p$
The output is the majority of the two initial signs and the block's majority sign
